massachusetts.state_note: Massachusetts DDS is part of MassAbility (formerly the Massachusetts Rehabilitation Commission) and is 100% funded by the Social Security Administration, with offices in Everett (Boston area) and Worcester.

michigan.state_note: Michigan's DDS sits in the Department of Health and Human Services and also decides State Disability Assistance and Medicaid disability claims, with offices in Lansing, Detroit, Kalamazoo, and Traverse City; Michigan adds a small state supplement to SSI ($14/month for a person living alone in 2026).

minnesota.state_note: Minnesota's DDS is housed in the Department of Employment and Economic Development (DEED) in St. Paul and is 100% federally funded; Mid-Minnesota Legal Aid is contracted with the Minnesota Department of Human Services to provide free Social Security advocacy, including SSI/SSDI applications, appeals, and hearing representation.

mississippi.state_note: Mississippi's DDS is a single office in Madison under the Mississippi Department of Rehabilitation Services and handles claims from all 23 Social Security field offices in the state; the Mississippi Center for Legal Services lists Social Security Disability and SSI among its case priorities.

missouri.state_note: Missouri's DDS sits under the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education's Office of Adult Learning and Rehabilitation Services, with six offices statewide. Missouri is a 209(b) state, so an SSI approval does not automatically enroll a person in MO HealthNet; a separate Medicaid application is required.

montana.state_note: Montana's DDS (also called the Disability Determination Bureau) is part of the Disability Employment and Transitions Division in the Department of Public Health and Human Services, with a single office in Helena; Montana Legal Services Association lists Social Security Disability among the free civil legal help it provides statewide.

nebraska.state_note: Nebraska's DDS is a division of the Nebraska Department of Education, with a single office in Lincoln. Nebraska pays a state supplement to SSI through the Assistance to the Aged, Blind, or Disabled (AABD) program, run separately from SSA by the Department of Health and Human Services.

nevada.dds_name: Nevada Disability Determination Services (Bureau of Disability Adjudication)
nevada.state_note: Nevada's DDS is called the Bureau of Disability Adjudication and sits in the Department of Employment, Training, and Rehabilitation (DETR), with offices in Carson City and Las Vegas; Nevada Legal Services is a statewide nonprofit that lists Social Security Disability among the government-benefit denials it handles.

new hampshire.state_note: New Hampshire's DDS is administered by the New Hampshire Department of Education, with a single office in Concord. New Hampshire Legal Assistance lists SSDI and SSI denials among the public-benefits cases it handles, and the state also offers Aid to the Permanently and Totally Disabled (APTD) cash assistance for residents ages 18-64.

new jersey.dds_name: New Jersey Division of Disability Determination Services
new jersey.state_note: New Jersey's Division of Disability Determination Services sits in the Department of Labor and Workforce Development and says an initial decision usually takes three to five months. New Jersey adds a small state supplement to SSI that Social Security pays with the federal check, and SSI recipients in New Jersey automatically receive Medicaid.
